sub: Named for its meaning, “sincerity” or pure oneness; the word itself isn’t in it
theme: The purest statement of who Allah is: One, the Master all creation turns to in need, with no child, no parent and no equal. It rules out every form of shirk.
story: Reports differ on the occasion. The idolaters of Makkah reportedly said: “Tell us the lineage of your Lord.” Other reports say Jewish rabbis, Christians of Najrān or others asked what He is like, or what He is made of: gold, silver or iron.
So some say it is Makkan and some Madinan. One way to reconcile the reports: it came early in Makkah, and the Prophet ﷺ recited it again whenever the same question was asked.
The Prophet ﷺ said it equals a third of the Quran. When a man recited it in every prayer because he loved it, he told him: “Your love of it will admit you to Paradise.”

sections.title: He is Allah, the One
sections.meaning: Say: He is Allah, One. Allah, aṣ-Ṣamad: the Master everyone depends on, while He depends on no one. He has no child and was not born. And nothing is equal or comparable to Him.
points: Allah, aṣ-Ṣamad: all depend on Him
He has no child and was not born
sections.matters: Tawḥīd is the foundation of the faith, and this surah states it in four short lines anyone can memorise. The Prophet ﷺ called it equal to a third of the Quran and recited it for protection morning, evening and before sleep.
sections.story: People asked the Prophet ﷺ to describe his Lord: His lineage, or what He is made of. Reports name the idolaters of Makkah, Jewish rabbis or Christians of Najrān. This surah was the answer.
explained: Aḥad means One with no partner, no parts and nothing resembling Him; no one else is called aḥad in this sense. Aṣ-Ṣamad is the perfect Master to whom all creation turns with every need, who needs no one, and who remains after everything else ends.

Lam yalid wa lam yūlad: He has no child, answering those who said the angels are His daughters or that ʿUzayr or ʿĪsā is His son. And He was not born, for whatever is born dies and leaves an inheritance. Kufuwan aḥad: none is His equal in names, attributes or actions.
teaches: Know Allah by how He describes Himself.
Turn to Allah alone for every need.
Allah has no child, no parent and no partner.
Love this surah and recite it often.
sections.hook: Aḥad appears in the first and last ayah. Allah’s name comes twice (1, 2). Ayah 3 pairs two denials, lam yalid / lam yūlad, and ayah 4 adds a third lam.

groups.text: He is Allah, the One; Allah, the Master everyone turns to in need.
He has no child, was not born, and nothing is equal to Him.

1.explain: Qul: say it, as a message to be conveyed. Aḥad: uniquely One, with no partner, no parts, and nothing like Him.
1.why: The idolaters reportedly said: “Tell us the lineage of your Lord.” Other reports name Jewish rabbis or Christians of Najrān asking what He is like or what He is made of.

2.explain: Aṣ-Ṣamad: the Master perfect in every quality, to whom all creation turns in every need, while He needs no one. Other meanings given: He does not eat or drink, and He remains after all else perishes.

3.explain: Lam yalid: He has no child, rejecting claims that the angels are His daughters or that ʿUzayr or ʿĪsā is His son. Lam yūlad: He was not born, for whatever is born will die.

4.explain: Kufuwan aḥad: none is equal or comparable to Him. No one is like Him in His names, attributes or actions, and no one ever will be.
